entry_points.text: Boot and zone setup entries: init empty zones, build and verify zonelists with boot pcp values, query local memory node, and reset node and zone structures for hotplug reuse.

Hotplug entries: online frame ranges with zone selection and present-count upkeep, init and tear down self-hosted maps, mark sections offline, bring nodes online, add plain or driver-managed ranges, query self-hosted support, and offline ranges.
Reclaim and writeback entries: recompute dirty limits with per-CPU ratelimit floor, start the per-node reclaim thread once, and detach reclaimable composites from LRU under lock.

exports.text: Hotplug node and range interface: bring nodes online, query self-hosted map support, add plain or driver-managed ranges in resource or address form, and offline managed ranges.

Core reuse and tuning helpers: node reset, boot pcp binding, LRU detach, cache setup, watermark and reserve work, unisolate and putback, range release, shuffling, stat thresholds, and reclaim thread start.

hazards.text: Guard a zero automatic ratio against division by zero, warn once on empty or misaligned online ranges, and handle nodes without online memory during rebuild. Refresh pcp tunables after watermark changes, split large buddies across isolate transitions, restrict shuffles to equal order, zone, buddy state and migrate type, and bound random partner search.

Hotplug failures include allocation exhaustion, null node, misaligned or empty ranges, unknown group or impossible node, arch or device errors with staged rollback, partial per-block state unwound on error, busy pinned pages, pending-signal interruption, notifier vetoes, and unresolved isolation or migration with rate-limited diagnostics.

invariants.text: Early boot has two builds for deferral and logging. One never defers; the other refuses with extensions or short ranges, starts after about one section, and records first deferred frame on section boundary. Free lists init heads, zero counts, plus unaccepted list when enabled. Diagnostics log conditionally or no-op.

Movable placement keeps kernel versus movable tallies, treats movable zone as movable with reservation adjustment, derives group demand from a percentage ratio, admits only when global and optional node-local ratio holds, scans low zones for default kernel fit, forces kernel on static kernel or mixed sections, and inherits a uniquely intersecting zone.

Zonelists append per-node refs in node order with null terminator, include only populated zones high to low, and record highest populated type. One build orders nodes by distance with round-robin adjustment and builds fallback plus local lists; the other builds single-node fallback. Mobility grouping follows excess over high watermark against one pageblock per type.

Per-CPU caches clear structures, init locks and lists, and install boot batch and high before tuned values; live updates propagate to all possible CPUs with ordered writes. Batch derives from managed pages versus 256KiB with anti-alias rounding, or one without translation. High derives from low watermark or managed fraction, split across node-local CPUs, clamped to four times batch.

Reserves spread a global kilobyte reserve by managed share excluding high and movable, which get small capped reserves; low, high and promotion add the larger of quarter share and scaled fraction. Global reserve scales with free buffers via root and clamps unless user value wins. Stat thresholds scale with CPUs and 128MiB units to a cap with drift marks. Node unmapped and slab minima accumulate zone shares by ratio.

Node reuse refreshes internals, allocates stats when on boot instance, zeroes counts and spans, folds deltas, and empties zones. Add needs non-empty block-aligned ranges; offline needs pageblock-aligned start, section-aligned end, no holes, single zone, and self-hosted whole-block coverage with payload. Self-hosted needs runtime switch, aligned sizes, and arch acceptance. Onlining rebuilds zonelists and counts when newly populated.

Shuffling randomizes free lists at fixed block order, aligns the zone interval, validates block heads, makes bounded random attempts for distinct partners, skips mismatched migrate types, swaps membership, and is gated by a static key with an empty alternate build.
Helpers outside this dossier are used only as opaque interfaces for alignment, strings, pages, nodes, CPUs, locks, warnings, and firmware; internals were not read here.

locks.text: Onlining mutates the isolated-block count under the zone lock with interrupts saved. Zonelist rebuilds hold the update sequence lock for writing with interrupts saved and use deferred printing. Deferred-init statics are unlocked as very early single-threaded state.
Watermark recomputation serializes globally with a private spinlock then refreshes cache tuning under a batch mutex; per-zone watermark fields mutate under the zone lock interrupt-safe.

Isolate release uses a scoped zone-lock guard and putback asserts it held; shuffling holds it interrupt-safe with periodic drop and yield. Hotplug pairs begin and end plus a device guard, protects isolated-count fixes with zone exclusion and LRU detach with reclaim locking, and disables pcp and reclaim caches across isolation.

state_machines.text: Online notifications move from going-online to online on success or cancel-online on failure; first memory on a node adds adding-first-memory to added-first-memory or its cancel, with rollback removing the range from the zone.

Node bring-up is idempotent with already-online success or init with exhaustion on failure. Range addition validates, resolves group node, guards, ensures node init, branches to per-block descriptors or plain insertion, links blocks, records firmware state, merges, and onlines blocks; failures unwind devices, arch state, descriptors, registration, and recording.

Offlining validates granularity and residency, disables caches, isolates, notifies, then loops scan, migrate, dissolve huge, and retest until stable before removing pages and fixing counts. Scan reports reclaim-tracked, movable-op, or migratable huge frames, rejects pinned offline frames as busy, and skips huge spans; migration isolates, gathers, moves with hotplug reason, and returns survivors on failure.

Isolate release expands to pageblock boundaries, skips blocks without isolated pages, decrements zone isolated count, and either splits a spanning large buddy or migrates free pages before toggling flags, warning on mismatch. Clearing isolate extracts a large buddy when present for later merging or uses the generic unisolate path, then clears the flag and queues the page at the free-list tail.

structs.text: Movable census holds early-kernel and movable counts, with group required-kernel demand. Observed state adds pcp cache with lock, lists, batch and high; zone with pcp pointers, tunables, watermark array with boost, isolated count and drift mark; node with zonelists, zones, reclaim thread, and unmapped and slab minima; and per-CPU stat thresholds.

Node descriptor carries identity, zone array and count, reclaim cursors, span and residency, per-CPU stats, reclaim and allocation waits with throttling, and a reclaim vector. Zone descriptor carries residency, node link, name, exclusion lock, pcp and stats pointers, high and batch tunables, and isolated-block count.

Hotplug uses a per-block descriptor with base and end frames and free count, linked from a block device holding the onlining mode; creation duplicates a template per block for arch insertion and device setup, and removal clears links then tears down devices, arch state, and descriptors.

ABI vocabulary covers movable versus kernel zones up to normal, explicit kernel and movable online types with automatic ratio policy, going-online, online and cancel stages plus first-memory node stages and memory states, numeric threshold and reserve bounds with batch and high relations, and distinct negative results for exhaustion, invalid, busy, absence, and interrupted.
